At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating to fundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for twoResearch Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order is transformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules and institutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes these processes as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating, reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutional arrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how such constellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce, transform, or erode.Job descriptionThe successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:- an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or- a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within a particular field, such as security, economy, or technology.Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.The doctoral researchers will:- develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;- conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;- contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;- participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;- present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;- contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.Your profile- An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis- A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies- A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)- A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods- Excellent written and spoken English- Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets- The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environmentWe offer- An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere- A varied, responsible and team-orientated job- Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)- Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases- A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces- A job ticket for public transport- Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centresApplicationThe Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system (https://jobs.mpil.de/3vrp7) available on our website by 22 November 2026.Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearly relates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendationThe documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early December in person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expenses cannot be covered.For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de (https://mailto:friedrichs@mpil.de) .

jobs.occupation: Rare Disease Manager (Key Account Manager) for NF1, Middle East of Germany (all genders) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Work Your Magic with us!Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology and Fertility. Our teams work together across 6 continents with passion and relentless curiosity in order to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team is becoming part of a diverse, inclusive and flexible working culture, presenting great opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe.Your Role: As a Rare Disease Manager (Key Account Manager) for Neurofibromatose Typ 1 (NF1) , you will be at the heart of transforming how patients with rare diseases access life-changing therapies — your work directly influences treatment pathways and outcomes for some of the most underserved patient populations. You will own your territory like a true entrepreneur, taking full accountability for strategy, execution, and sustainable business growth across hospitals, treatment centers, and referral networks. You will develop and execute customized strategic account plans that strengthen centers of excellence, optimize referral pathways, and accelerate time-to-treatment for patients in need. Building deep, trust-based partnerships with physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and multidisciplinary teams will be your daily currency — and you will do it with scientific credibility and genuine care. Leveraging your deep scientific expertise, you will engage healthcare professionals as a peer and trusted partner, translating complex clinical evidence into meaningful conversations that drive better standards of care. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional colleagues in Medical Affairs, Market Access, Marketing, and Commercial teams to align strategies and maximize impact across the healthcare ecosystem. Data is your compass: you will use CRM tools, market analytics, and territory business planning to identify opportunities, monitor performance, and continuously refine your approach. You will champion disease awareness and patient education initiatives, playing a key role in shaping the rare disease landscape in your region. Acting as the voice of the customer, you will bring actionable field insights back to the organization — directly influencing strategy at a national level. This is a rare opportunity to combine commercial excellence with genuine patient impact — if that drives you, this role was made for you.Your territory covers key hubs across the Middle East of Germany — mainly Dresden, Leipzig and Göttingen area — and ideally, you already call one of these regions home.Who You Are:- You hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Biology, Chemistry, Pharmacy, Medicine, or a related life science field; a qualification as Pharmaceutical Representative per local regulatory requirements is a plus.- You bring at least 4–5 years of commercial experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, or healthcare industry, with a proven track record in strategic account management and market development.- You have hands-on experience in rare disease environments and a strong understanding of the complex stakeholder dynamics involved.- You possess deep knowledge of healthcare systems, reimbursement pathways, and patient access processes, ideally with exposure to high-cost specialty therapies.- You are scientifically agile — able to engage with complex clinical data and translate it into compelling, compliant customer discussions.- You combine an entrepreneurial mindset with strong analytical capabilities, taking ownership of results and thriving in ambiguous, fast-evolving environments.- You are a skilled communicator and relationship builder, experienced in working across cross-functional teams and navigating complex stakeholder landscapes.- You are fluent in German and English and highly willing to travel within your territory, including overnight travel as required.- A valid driving license is required.What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

jobs.description: About usAirbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.Job descriptionIn order to support Earth Observation & Science projects within Space Systems, Airbus Defence and Space in Ottobrunn is looking for anOptical Architect (d/f/m)You will join a multicultural team of engineers specialized in the development of optical (sub-)systems working for Earth Observation & Science projects within Space Systems. These developments cover instruments for ESA, CNES, DLR and EU programmes across the spectral range from ultraviolet to thermal infrared. Examples include LIDARs (ATLID, MERLIN), Multi-Spectral Instruments (Sentinel-2 MSI, Sentinel-4, Sentinel-5) from the Copernicus programme, infrared instruments (LSTM, TRISHNA), meteorological instruments (IASI-NG and METimage) embarked on MetOp-SG, instruments for scientific missions like EUCLID, cameras embarked on LEO and GEO satellites, and national programmes.This role is also available with reduced weekly hours and an adapted scope of tasks.Your locationOur site is just a stone's throw away from Munich, the beautiful capital of Bavaria.Are you into sports and other outdoor activities? The Alps and Lake Starnberg are within an hour’s reach, offering a multitude of recreational options.Our Benefits for You- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.Your tasks and responsibilities- Define and develop optical subsystem architecture and verification strategies for space-borne instruments in project phases B2, C, and D following defined processes.- Act as the main technical contact point for optical domain matters, supporting systems engineers on technological, design, verification, risk, cost, and schedule aspects.- Perform optical design and analysis, including stray light analysis, optical layout, tolerances, and stray light, thermal, and optical performance (STOP) budget allocations.- Coordinate optical subsystem engineering and Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) activities across multidisciplinary teams (Mechanical, Thermal, Electrical, Detection-chain, Cleanliness).- Derive, consolidate, and maintain optical subsystem requirements in alignment with higher-level specifications (e.g., SRD, IRD) and verification plans.- Oversee subcontracted optical equipment procurement, reviewing data packages and test plans to ensure on-time, on-cost, and on-quality delivery.- Contribute to future programmes (phase 0 or A/B1), support internal/external R&D proposals for new optical technologies, and participate in lessons-learnt exchanges.Desired skills and qualifications- Master's degree or PhD in Physics, Optical Engineering- Proven multi-year experience in optical instrumentation or optical sensors, ideally for space applications- Solid experience in optical layout, design, tolerance, and STOP analysis, including maintenance of optical allocations/budgets.- Proficiency with commercial optical design software (e.g., Code V, Zemax, FRED) and programming languages (e.g., Matlab, Python).- Sound technical knowledge of optical components (e.g., mirrors, photonics, gratings, fibers, lasers, coatings) and space equipment alignment/testing strategies.- Strong communication skills, collaborative problem-solving approach, and experience in managing suppliers or subcontractors.- Professional working proficiency in English; knowledge of German is beneficial.Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.Take your career to a new level and apply online now!This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growthBy submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We, the Max Planck Institute for Medical Research, are one of 85 institutes and research centers of the Max Planck Society (MPG) for the advancement of science. Our focus is on basic medical research. We currently employ around 270 people in science and administration, mainly at our location in Heidelberg. Another location for our institute is currently being established in Heilbronn. We are also part of the Health + Life Science Alliance Heidelberg Mannheim, an association of the region's leading life science research institutions.The MPG strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. As the MPG has set itself the goal of employing more people with severe disabilities, applications from people with severe disabilities are expressly welcome. In addition, the MPG wants to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore expressly encouraged to apply.The female reproductive tract is a highly dynamic system in which tissue mechanics, active forces, and fluid flow interact with cellular and physiological processes. Yet, how these physical properties contribute to reproductive function remains poorly understood.Within the ERC Starting Grant project REPROMECH – Quantitative Mechanics of the Oviduct: Force, Flow, and the Physiological Operating Point, our group investigates how forces and mechanical properties shape the function of the female reproductive system. We combine approaches from reproductive biology, mechanobiology, and experimental biophysics to quantitatively characterize living tissues across cellular and tissue scales.The doctoral project will investigate the mechanical properties of the female reproductive tract and their relationship to tissue function.Tasks- Quantification of mechanical properties of the female reproductive tract using complementary mechanical measurements and advanced microscopy- Preparation and culture of ex vivo tissue samples- Histological characterization of biological samples- Quantitative image and data analysis- Critical analysis and interpretation of experimental resultsProfile- You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in reproductive biology, developmental biology, biology, biophysics, physics, bioengineering, biomedical engineering, biotechnology, or a related discipline.- We are looking for a candidate with strong experimental aptitude, excellent practical laboratory skills, manual dexterity, and a quantitative and analytical mindset.- You should enjoy technically demanding experimental work, be able to interpret complex data critically and rigorously, and be motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries.- Willingness to work with laboratory mice and to complete the required laboratory-animal training is essential.- Previous experience in reproductive biology, experimental biophysics, microscopy, or work with laboratory animals is advantageous but not required. Coordinate procurementactivities, oversee contractor performance, and ensure projectdeliverables meet specifications. As a hands-on mechanical engineer, you'll work oneverything from equipment design to production support. Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in MechanicalEngineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, orrelated technical field. Strong foundation in equipment maintenance,reliability engineering, and manufacturing processes. Knowledge offood industry applications preferred. Technical Skills: Knowledge ofmanufacturing processes and production optimization techniques,familiarity with lean manufacturing principles. Strong troubleshootingabilities with hands-on experience developing mechanical solutions anddiagnosing and repairing mechanical equipment failures. Proficiencywith CAD software, process modeling tools, and manufacturing softwaresystems. Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solvingabilities with experience in root cause analysis and processtroubleshooting. Operational Agility:A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to adaptquickly in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment. LanguageProficiency: Fluency in English and/or German, with professional levelin the later, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.Why us? jobs.description: As a Senior AI Solution Architect in our Forward Deployed Engineering team, you see the whole board before a single line of code is written. You partner directly with business leaders across Siemens to map complex challenges to existing data, design cross-platform architectures spanning cloud and enterprise systems, and make critical build-versus-buy decisions in days rather than quarters. You bridge deep technical AI expertise with systems thinking, acting as a force multiplier that enables agile engineering teams to deliver high-impact solutions reliably and repeatedly.What we offer you:- An attractive remuneration package- Access to Siemens share plans- 30 days of paid vacation and a variety of flexible work schedules that allow time off for you and your family- Flexible training opportunities for both your professional and personal development that you can tailor to your interestsSince each of over 300,000 team members feels that other benefits are particularly important, and we cannot list our entire benefit portfolio here, you can find more information here (https://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs/benefits-what-we-offer.html) .The individual benefits are subject to regulatory, contractual, or corporate conditions.You’ll make an impact by:- Driving rapid solution architecture as the first technical expert in every engagement, translating complex business problems into viable technical blueprints within days. - Designing interconnected solutions across the entire enterprise landscape, leveraging SDC for workloads while integrating seamlessly with SAP, Salesforce, and cloud-native services. - Owning crucial architecture decisions regarding cost, latency, scalability, and stack selection, while documenting clear justifications for every trade-off. - Evaluating emerging AI technologies with rigorous skepticism, providing evidence-backed adoption recommendations and having the courage to say "not ready yet." - Staying actively involved in the codebase through technical spikes, prototype development, and pull-request reviews to ensure your architectures remain grounded in reality. - Designing from day one for seamless handover, establishing explicit interface contracts, evaluation harnesses, and operational runbooks so domain teams can run systems autonomously.Your defining qualities:- Education: You hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI/ML, or a comparable quantitative field, where a proven track record of shipped systems outweighs advanced degrees. - Experience & Skills:- You bring 8 or more years of experience in software architecture, AI/ML systems design, or solution architecture, including at least 3 years focused on complex enterprise AI solutions. - You demonstrate a robust history of customer-facing delivery and technical leadership, especially when navigating demanding or high-pressure stakeholder environments. - You posses hands-on coding capabilities in Python alongside TypeScript or JavaScript, allowing you to write production-grade code and build functional prototypes. - You provide expertise in cross-platform system design by successfully integrating disparate enterprise environments like SAP, Salesforce, and modern cloud services. - You exhibit deep knowledge of the modern AI stack, covering LLM failure modes, RAG architectures, evaluation metrics, vector stores, and prominent agent frameworks. - You bring working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider (Azure, AWS, or GCP) sufficient to design scalable multi-platform workloads.- Ways of working:- You demonstrate the critical ability to evaluate emerging technologies objectively, separate genuine value from hype, and communicate technical realities clearly. - You display exceptional live communication skills to sketch defensible architectures in real-time meetings and explain them fluently in business terms.- Languages: You have fluent English language skills, complemented by strong German proficiency as an advantageous asset for local stakeholder engagements.You are much more than your qualifications, and we believe in the potential of every single candidate. We look forward to getting to know you!At Siemens, we believe that feeling valued and included is the foundation for doing great work. That’s why we aim to create an inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, and where individual perspectives and experiences are celebrated. Our commitment to fairness and respect extends to every applicant.As an equal opportunity employer (http://www.siemens.com/global/en/company/sustainability/social-commitments/belonging.html) , we welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from persons with disabilities.About usWe know that our business thrives only when our people thrive and unlock their full potential. That’s why you are always our top priority. Our global, diverse team is ready to support, challenge, and inspire you, helping you grow in countless ways. Together, we’ll embark on an exciting journey of discovery. Who knows where this path will lead? Join us and take an active role in shaping your future!www.siemens.de/careers (http://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs.html) – if you would like to find out more about jobs & careers at Siemens.FAQ (https://www.siemens.com/en-us/company/jobs/faq/) – if you need further information on the application process.

jobs.description: At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.The PositionASPIRE is a multi-year program that will define, design, and deploy Future ERP solutions based on SAP S/4 HANA and other cloud/on-premise technology platforms. The program will enable simplified, standardized, and harmonized global business processes by capitalizing on SAP, Life Science Industry and Roche effective practices.The opportunity: * Preparation and leading of FIT-to-Template (assessment of the current business processes compared and aligned against the future Aspire Global Template) and scoping workshops for Financial Compliance* Liaising with local affiliate Finance stakeholders for the implementation of Financial Compliance requirements* Assessment of localization requirements for Authorization* Execution of Testing Activities during the deployment (UT, SAT, UAT, REG)* Go Live & Hyper care (incl. Month end closing) support* Ensure template governance within the project including change control management in line with the respective GBPMs/GBPOs and the overall Finance governance conceptWho you are* You have a university degree in Business Administration, Accounting or a related field.* 5+ years related business experience or equivalent Project Management skills in the area of SAP Authorization* Broad knowledge of business processes, policies and programs* Strong Project Management, business partner management, communication and change management skills. Experience in Agile Project Methodologies is a plus* Strong people skills are required as the role is highly consultative, interacting with staff at all levels across an organization * Proficiency in EnglishIn exchange we provide you with:* Development opportunities: Roche is rich in learning resources. We provide constant development opportunities, free language courses & trainings, the possibility of international assignments, internal position changes and the chance to shape your own career. * Excellent benefits & flexibility:  competitive salary and cafeteria package, language allowance (if the position requires extra language), annual bonus, Private Medical Services, Employee Assistance Program, All You Can Move Sportpass, coaching / mentoring opportunity, buddy program, team buildings, holiday party. We also ensure flexibility, to help you find your balance: home office is a common practice (2 office days/week on average).  We create the opportunity for freedom in working, where your corporate and private life coexist in harmony.* A global inclusive community, where we learn from each other. At Roche, we cooperate, debate, make decisions, celebrate successes and have fun as a team. Our leadership is very focused on people, creating a strong, inclusive culture, so you always have the chance to share your opinion.Duration: This position is temporary for 2 years.So far, so good?It gets even better. In the role of RDT Business Partner at Roche Digital Technology (RDT) / Informatics, you will make a decisive contribution to turning our vision "Doing now what patients need next" into reality. You are part of RDT Pharma International and belong to the RDT Business Partner team at the preferred location in Grenzach. Here, we combine technological innovation with commercial goals to continuously improve patient care through digital solutions and actively shape the healthcare ecosystem.Responsibilities | What awaits youIn this role, you will take responsibility for the strategic connection between Roche Digital Technology (RDT) and the assigned business functions to advance Roche's strategic goals through groundbreaking technology solutions. In addition, you will take on the following exciting tasks:* Stakeholder Management: You act as a trusted strategic partner and advisor to business leaders, co-create technology-enabled strategies, and proactively drive global process improvements.* Bridge between Local & Global: You bundle the local requirements of the business functions (Commercial, Finance, P&C, Supply Chain, etc.), advocate for local needs at the global level when necessary, and conversely bring global standard solutions effectively to Germany.* Innovation & Impact: You specifically identify business opportunities and work closely with Product Leads to design, prototype, and continuously develop innovative technological capabilities.* Complexity Management: You are accountable for the successful delivery of technology-enabled business outcomes (such as annual revenue goals or patient access) for commercial areas.* Problem Solving: In strong partnership with Product Engineering Teams, you are responsible for the escalation and targeted resolution of complex, systemic challenges.* Technology Focus: As a Key Opinion Leader, you drive the technological vision forward, manage stakeholders end-to-end, and scale pilot solutions to maximize their added value.Qualifications | Who you areFor this demanding interface role, you bring sound IT knowledge, strong business acumen, and excellent communication skills:* Education: Successfully completed Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field; a Master’s degree or MBA is a plus.* Professional Experience & Industry Knowledge: Sound experience participating in IT projects within complex matrix organizations as well as strong business acumen in the pharmaceutical / life sciences environment.* Partnership & Moderation: Proven track record of building trusted relationships across different organizational levels (including management level), as well as strong competence in conflict management and moderating complex interfaces.* Language & Communication Skills: You bring excellent communication skills (fluent/negotiating-level English for collaboration in a global environment as well as very good German skills for daily interaction at the Grenzach site).* Working Style & Presence: High flexibility, strong analytical skills, and systems thinking, as well as the willingness for on-site presence at the Grenzach location.* Teamwork: Strong ability to collaborate constructively in cross-functional, agile teams and to actively promote appreciative cooperation.Duration: This position is a temporary assignment limited until January 2028.Your ApplicationWe ask you for a current CV and your official (educational) certificates/proofs. Your contact to us! With people. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.Let’s build a healthier future, together.Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.occupation: PhD position (m/f/d) on immune reset through CAR T in chronic inflammatory diseases (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: State-of-the-art medicine and nursing care you can rely on! - Since being founded in 1815, Universitätsklinikum Erlangen has offered medicine of the highest standard and incorporated the latest insights from medical research and state-of-the-art equipment into diagnosis and therapy. More than 10.000 employees from approximately 50 different occupations are needed to provide the wide range of services offered by Universitätsklinikum Erlangen, ensuring our patients receive the very best care around the clock.As a PhD student, you will investigate how human immune-cell networks shape tissue inflammation, regeneration and response to cellular therapies. The project will focus primarily on the human immune system and combine patient-derived material with experimental models to address mechanistic questions in cellular immunology.Your tasks:- Characterizing human immune-cell populations and their functional states using multiparameter flow cytometry and high-dimensional immune phenotyping.- Investigating cellular interactions and immune networks by integrating phenotypic, functional and molecular data from immune cells and tissues.- Studying immune responses to cellular therapies, including the mechanisms underlying immune depletion, reconstitution and tissue regeneration following CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Generating and analyzing molecular data using approaches such as bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and other transcriptomic or spatial technologies.- Establishing and applying experimental models to investigate mechanisms identified in human samples, including selected mouse models of intestinal inflammation, immune reconstitution and tissue regeneration after CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Developing and combining experimental and analytical approaches ranging from established methods such as ELISA, Western blotting and flow cytometry to advanced multidimensional cytometry, UMAP-based analysis and transcriptomic approaches.- The project offers substantial scope to develop an individual scientific profile. Previous experience with these techniques is welcome, but curiosity, scientific independence, willingness to learn, and enthusiasm for understanding how immune cells interact in human disease are similarly important.Essential experience/ qualifications:- Above the average motivation and work ethics- Strong theoretical and practical background in standard methods of molecular and cellular biology as well as cellular immunology- English writing and speaking skills- Ability to work together in a multi-national team that is supportive of one another- A master degree (M.Sc.) in immunology, biology, molecular biology, molecular medicine or equivalentadditional advantages:- Experience in omics data science- Hands-on experience in human immunologyWe offer:- The position is full-time and will be payed according to salary group TVL-E 13, 65% (DFG-typical rate)- Intended pay grade depending on qualifications and personal requierements- Initially, the position is limited for one year, with the possibility of an extension till the degreee is achieved- The head of the department guaranties in writing that there is funding till the degree is achieved.- Hiring process opened and will be completed asap.- An enthusiastic, interdisciplinary team of scientists and doctors- High end translational research- State-of-the-art laboratories- Two-Stepp mentoring with a hands-on mentor (post-doc) plus the PI as supervisor with high frequent project discussions for efficient development- Structured program for hard- and soft-skills in research (paper and grant writing classes, paper clubs, soft-skill training)- Notes for applicants (f/m/d) ( https://www.karriere.uk-erlangen.de/bewerbung/hinweise-fuer-bewerbende/ )- Comprehensive health promotion offers- All benefits of the public service incl. supplementary pension plan of the Versorgungsanstalt des Bundes und der Länder (VBL) (Federal and State Government Employees' Retierment Fund)- Family-friendly enviromentFurther information:Prof. Dr. med. habil. Fabian MüllerMedizinische Klinik 5Phone: 09131 - 85 43107Applications:Universitätsklinikum ErlangenMedizinische Klinik 5 -Hämatologie & Internistische OnkologiePD Dr. med. habil. Fabian MüllerUlmenweg 1891054 Erlangen

jobs.description: At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have been striving to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. It continues to drive innovation in software development, making thousands of programmers more productive every day. In addition to Java, IntelliJ IDEA includes various development tools for other prominent languages such as Ruby, Groovy, Scala, Python, JavaScript, Objective-C, PHP, and Kotlin.About the teamThe IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate team is responsible for supporting a wide range of enterprise frameworks, data-access stacks, and application servers in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate. This includes technologies such as Spring (including Spring Boot, Spring Data, Spring Security, and others), Jakarta EE, Quarkus, Micronaut, various reactive and data-access libraries, and popular application servers like Tomcat, WildFly, and Jetty. We ensure that developers can easily create, configure, run, debug, and observe their backend applications directly from the IDE. As part of the Ultimate QA group, you’ll work across different areas of the product – frameworks, HTTP client, persistence tooling, and application servers – and collaborate closely with developers, product managers, and other QA teams to deliver a smooth end-to-end experience for JVM backend developers.We’re now looking for a QA Automation Engineer to join the IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate QA team and help ensure the quality of a product that our customers and software engineers around the world rely on daily. You’ll work alongside QA engineers to design and set up our automation process for end-to-end tests, as well as implement and automate test scenarios that catch issues before they reach our users.What you’ll doCore responsibilities:- Design, develop, and maintain multi-platform and environmental (Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker, WSL) automated test scenarios.- Expand test coverage for new and existing functionality.- Debug and troubleshoot test failures.- Improve existing automation based on team feedback and reduce test flakiness.- Track quality metrics, including testing coverage, failure rate, and flakiness.- Contribute to frameworks and tools with product-specific extensions as needed.- Help the team monitor test execution results and investigate failures.- Participate in release quality assessments.- Collaborate with QA and developers to define test strategies.- Do manual QA activities when needed.- Participate in the test documentation creation.- Improve domain-specific test infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines within your team’s scope.- Share automation best practices with the team.- Work with the tooling team to adopt new frameworks and practices.What we’re looking forRequired skills:- Proven experience in test automation.- Solid programming skills in Kotlin/Java.- Experience with test frameworks like JUnit or TestNG.- Familiarity with build tools, like Maven and Gradle.- An understanding of software testing principles and methodologies.- Familiarity with CI/CD tools (TeamCity or similar).- Experience with reporting tools (Allure or others).- Version control experience (Git).- Proficiency in spoken and written English.- Responsibility, self-discipline, and self-learning skills.- Strong teamwork skills.- The ability to work independently, creatively, and on your own initiative.Nice to have:- Experience testing developer tools, IDEs, and desktop applications.- Familiarity with JVM Frameworks (Spring or Jakarta) and databases.**Why join JetBrains?** - About JetBrainsWe create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.What you’ll doWe build Qodana to bring the intelligence of JetBrains IDEs directly into the CI/CD pipeline, helping engineering teams spot security flaws, license issues, and bugs before they ever reach production. As AI-assisted coding grows, the need for deep, static code analysis is more critical than ever.In this role, you’ll join our Qodana Core team to expand our static analysis engine and design new algorithms for complex, inter-procedural code analysis. You will have direct ownership over how we configure and orchestrate these analyses across different environments. You’ll collaborate closely with other JetBrains compiler and IDE teams, directly influencing how development teams worldwide maintain code quality and adopt AI safely.Day to day, you will:- Design and implement new static analysis checks, rules, and inter-procedural analysis algorithms.- Extend Qodana’s capabilities in critical areas like license compliance, security, and vulnerability detection.- Optimize how code analysis runs, configure execution paths, and orchestrate performance based on project context.- Build and refine CI/CD integrations to make Qodana easy to adopt across different development workflows.- Collaborate with compiler and IDE teams across JetBrains to share insights and align analysis engines.- Take ownership of features from early concept to release, gathering feedback and iterating to make them better.What you’ll bring- A deep curiosity about code structure, compilers, and how static analysis works.- A proactive mindset, not waiting for permission to fix a broken process or improve a system.- Strong collaboration skills and a readiness to support your technical ideas with clear, logical reasoning.- Comfort working in a distributed team across different countries and time zones.- A focus on quality over quick fixes, valuing long-term maintainability in your work.- Experience with developer tooling, static analysis, application security, or LLM-based applications would be a plus. Familiarity with languages and ecosystems beyond the JVM – such as C++, Rust, JavaScript or TypeScript, Python, .NET, or Go – would also be valuable.What you’ll need- Deep, practical knowledge of JVM development (such as Kotlin or Java).- Experience designing and implementing complex algorithms or handling performance-critical backend architectures.- Fluent communication skills in English to collaborate with team members globally.What success looks like- **First 3 months:** You will get familiar with the Qodana codebase and the IntelliJ Platform architecture, delivering your first set of analysis rules and integrations.- **First 6 months:** You will take full ownership of specific analysis features, collaborating with neighboring teams to design robust solutions for complex codebases.- **Long term:** You will help shape the technical direction of Qodana Core, continuously raising the bar for static analysis performance and developer experience.Why join JetBrains?- Strong base salary – We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience.- Flexible work schedule – Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office.- Extra time off – More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.- Learning and development opportunities – Access to conferences, courses, and language classes.- Relocation support – Assistance to help make your move as smooth and stress-free as possible.- Free meals and snacks – Lunch and refreshments provided to keep you fueled.- Health and wellness – On-site gyms or sports club stipends.- Internal events – Company-wide celebrations and team gatherings.We are an equal opportunity employer. We know great ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. That’s why we do our best to create an open and inclusive workplace – one that welcomes everyone regardless of their background, identity, religion, age, accessibility needs, or orientation.If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.Ergänzende Informationen:Nur schwerbehinderte oder ihnen gleichgestellte PersonenHomeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day Join us as an EHS Manager (f/m/d), where you will play a pivotal role in supporting and advising the GT Transformer business on essential environmental, health, and safety (EHS) requirements. Imagine driving initiatives that foster a culture of safe behavior and helping us climb the safety culture ladder. You will lead training initiatives within the EQS team, ensuring continuous improvement under our Zero Harm framework and integrated management systems, particularly focusing on ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards. Your analytical skills will shine as you track incident statistics and support root cause analyses, all while promoting regulatory compliance and closing any gaps.How You’ll Make an Impact * Drive initiatives to enhance a culture of safety within the organization* Lead and support necessary EHS training initiatives to promote awareness and compliance* Analyze EHS data and report incident statistics to identify trends and areas for improvement* Provide guidance on environmental, health, and safety issues, ensuring regulatory compliance* Facilitate regular meetings within the EQS community to promote information exchange and updates* Support root cause analysis of EHS events and track identified actions for continuous improvementWhat You Bring* A Bachelor’s degree in a technical field such as engineering, industrial engineering, or environmental engineering* Several years of EHS experience in manufacturing or a related industry, ideally within Grid Technologies* Strong communication skills, akin to those of an influencer or salesperson, to effectively promote safety culture* Training as a specialist in occupational safety is a significant advantage* Experience in high-risk activities such as cranes & lifting, machine guarding, and energy isolation* Proficiency in EHS management systems (ISO 14001; ISO 45001) and skills in auditing and root cause investigation* Good written and spoken German and English skills, with a willingness to travel occasionallyAbout the TeamOur Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day The growing number of decentralized renewables is making it much more difficult to ensure reliable and stable grid operation. Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) are the perfect solution for increasing the reliability of AC grids, ensuring stability, and boosting transmission efficiency. Siemens Energy supports customers around the world with innovative FACTS to help them master the challenges of energy transitions. But honestly, we can’t do it alone! Transforming the entire energy system requires you to play a part.How You’ll Make an Impact * You will develop FACTS turnkey projects from the first idea in customers mind till successful signature. These projects can be several hundred millions worth.* Your prime task will be technical sales for the global market for STATCOM and E-STATCOM with supercapacitors, with special focus on eSTATCOM in the USA.* You will carry out pre-qualifications and provide budget offers.* You will prepare the sales strategy for projects including pricing.* You will also be in the lead to negotiating and successfully close the contracts together with our commercial experts.* Close cooperation with associated engineering, tender and project execution departments is the key to developing a tailored concept to the customers’ requirements as the basis for a successful project development.* During the whole time, you will build up and maintain relationships by making frequent visits to our worldwide customers' decision makers. You will also cooperate with our regional organization providing local support and customer intimacy.* As a technical sales expert, you will also consistently monitor market development in the assigned sales area and maintain the project lists on an ongoing basis.What You Bring* Master's degree in electrical engineering or industrial engineering, preferably with a focus on high-voltage engineering.* Long term sales experience in electrical energy transmission turnkey solution business.* Technical knowledge in the field of FACTS, especially power electronics based STATCOMS will be an absolute plus. * High‑voltage, control & protection or system‑design engineering experience, hands‑on control & protection commissioning will be an asset.* Strong know‑how in supercapacitors will be a major advantage in this role.* Willingness for international travel and visits to customers plant sites for up to 20%.* Experience in leading teams across country borders.* Comfortable in presenting in front of customers and internal top management. * Proficient in English. Additional German skills are a strong upside.  About the TeamOur Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  * We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.#LI-AB3https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 19 November 2026, stating the reference number Ref. #11-26021, including:- cover letter describing your motivation to apply for this position- detailed CV- contact details of two potential references- all academic credentials and certificatesPlease submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.If you have any specific questions about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Kastner at thomas.kastner@senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact xxxxx atvorname.nachname@senckenberg.deFor data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.Application documents will also be made available to members of the selection committee from Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE), solely for the purpose of assessing applications and selecting candidates.

Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its Department of River Ecology and Conservation in Gelnhausen, starting as soon as possible2 Postdoctoral Researchers (ecologists) (m/f/d)(full-time / part-time)Location: GelnhausenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options are availableType of contract: limited two years / an extension is be possibleRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) E 13Senckenberg is one of the world’s leading research institutions in the field of Biodiversity and Earth System Research, with eight research institutes and three natural history museums across Germany and scientists from over 40 nations. Our headquarter is located in the thriving commercial metropolis of Frankfurt in the heart of Germany, which also hosts one of our most famous facilities, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum. The location of the available position is in a Senckenberg institute about 40 kilometers east of Frankfurt in Gelnhausen, a historic town accessible via public transport (rail and bus).We are looking for enthusiastic ecologists with a background in broad-scale biodiversity change, community ecology, macroecology, metacommunities, and/or analysis of ecological time series.The two positions are embedded in one or more of the following projects:1. Synthesis Center on Freshwater Biodiversity Change in Europe The Synthesis Center brings together and supports a broad variety of researchers and practitioners investigating a broad variety of fundamental and applied ecological questions, with a particular focus on broad-scale and long-term biodiversity change, community ecology, freshwater ecology, time series analyses, multiple stressor impacts, and conservation (see doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06400-1 for an example). Data for > 30,000 freshwater biodiversity time series across 30 European countries have already been compiled from rivers and lakes, covering invertebrates, fish, macrophytes, diatoms, and benthic algae, in collaboration with a large pan-European network of > 200 researchers. Positions involved in this project are expected to pursue similar questions using the already available data.2. Positions involved in this project will focus on several tasks, including European-scale biodiversity data mobilization activities (e.g., tracking down datasets and preparing them for use), and the learning and deployment of field-based methods for data collection (e.g., Malaise traps). Participating researchers will gain experience in broad-scale biodiversity data collection and management, biodiversity monitoring, and participation in European-scale research networks.Your tasks• Contributing scientifically to one or more of the above-described projects (you can indicate a preference in your application if you have one)• Analyzing spatial and temporal biodiversity data, and accompanied environmental data, to elucidate spatial patterns and temporal trends and drivers thereof• Preparing scientific manuscripts• Attending project meetings and preparing project reports• Mentoring graduate students• Giving oral presentations at national and international conferences• Attending virtual and physical project meetingsYour profile• PhD in Ecology or a related field• Solid background in fields related to the above expected tasks for a given project or projects.• Advanced skills in statistical analyses, using R• Skills in project management and report writing are preferred but not essential• Strong publication record for your current career level• Excellent written and oral communication and project presentation skills in EnglishWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter outlining your suitability for the post, a detailed CV, contact details of 2 references, a list of publications and acquired funding electronically (as a single PDF) stating the **reference #04-26004 by November 22nd, 2026 **using the application form on our website https://www.senckenberg.de/de/karriere/ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.If you have any specific questions about this role position, please contact Prof. Dr. Peter Haase at peter.haase@senckenberg.de.

jobs.description: Create your own happiness!Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?What you can look forward to…The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term, but an extension is possible.Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the children (age 1-6) entrusted to us in line with our educational approach, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. In your daily work, you would speak mainly English.We would appreciate at least some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.The Team: One for all, all for one!Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.Has this piqued your curiosity? Then you should definitely keep reading…Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.Feel free to get to know us!The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 42-48 children are currently cared for by nine early childhood educators. jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de
