jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its institute Senckenberg am Meer, German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research in Hamburg, starting as soon as possibleResearch Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity(full time / part-time )Location: HamburgEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options availableType of contract: temporary contract limited until 30.09.2029Remuneration: collective agreement of the state Hesse, TV-H E13﻿The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.As part of the institute “Senckenberg am Meer” located in Wilhelmshaven, with its two departments Marine Research and German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research (DZMB), the Hamburg research site, which belongs to the DZMB, focuses on researching taxonomy and systematics of marine life forms.The position is based within the Zooplankton Working Group and is part of the joint project ZooM-In (Innovative Methods for National Zooplankton Monitoring), contributing to the further development and standardization of modern methods for marine biodiversity monitoring. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through the National Biodiversity Monitoring Centre’s initiative Sustainable Biodiversity Monitoring.The project will be carried out in close cooperation with the Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity (HIFMB) as well as federal and state authorities.Your tasks- Project management of the project ZooM-In- Organisation of and participation in monthly expeditions (March-October, 3-4 days per months) to the North Sea- Organisation of project workshops- Assessment of zooplankton biodiversity by imaging technologies- Cross validation of zooplankton biodiversity assessment by traditional microscopy, molecular genetics and imaging methods- Communication of project results to stakeholders- Publication of project results in peer-reviewed journals- Writing of a project reportYour profile- Master degree in marine biology or natural sciences- Expertise in the application of plankton imaging technologies (ZooScan and/or PlanktoScope)- Relevant knowledge on molecular genetic analyses of organisms, ideally metabarcoding of zooplankton- Experience in data analyses, preferably using R- Experience with sea-going expeditions on research vessels and sampling of plankton, resilience to motion sickness- Willingness to participate in interdisciplinary work- Very good communication skills, ability to work in a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary and international environment- Very good command of English (written and spoken)- Sound command of the German language is essential for this positionWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan- Senckenberg is committed to diversity. The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years; the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile - Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills - Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer - Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card  with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement  – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply? Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/)For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de (http://www.senckenberg.de)Contact Senckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 40%

jobs.occupation: 23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – HamburgResearchThe program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray scienceWe offer:- A range of PhD positions in these areas: open positions (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/350422/open_phd_projects)- State-of-the-art research facilities on an extensive science campus- Cross-disciplinary research in a vibrant, international scientific environment- First class supervision and mentorship by a team of internationally renowned experts- Outstanding training in your scientific subject and transferable skills (in English)- A 3-year employment contract based on the German federal pay agreementRequirementsWe seek applicants with an excellent academic background. You hold (or are about to complete) an MSc degree or equivalent in physics, chemistry or related areas. You need to be passionate about research in ultrafast phenomena and motivated to conduct rigorous scientific work over the full degree period.ApplyApplications must be submitted via the [online application portal](https://jobs.b-ite.com/en/jobposting/760bb8588f9051b5f5b84840eb91eff55142a8780/apply)The application deadline is 06th November 2026. PhD projects start in summer/autumn 2026. In exceptional cases, it may possible to start on the research project earlier. Your applicationPlease submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable.We look forward to receiving your application!Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.Your tasks•  Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil.•  Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses.•  Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility.•  Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico.•  Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings.Your qualifications•  Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field.•  Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided.•  Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning.•  Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research.•  Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English.•  Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite.We offer•  A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration.•  Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise.•  An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences.•  Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies.•  Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified.This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration.The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. jobs.occupation: Scientific Programmer (mfd) High-Performance Computing and Software Engineering (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology is a research institute of the Max Planck Society. It was founded in 1992 in the State of Bremen and employs around 200 staff members. In close collaboration with numerous university and non-university research institutions, we explore the diversity and function of microorganisms in the ocean and their interactions with their environment. Scientists from all over the world, engineers, technicians and administrative staff together make an important contribution to global marine and environmental research.In the Department of Ocean Biosphere Dynamics, we are looking to fill up a position asScientific Programmer (mfd)High-Performance Computing and Software EngineeringThe department investigates the dynamics of the ocean carbon cycle, its variability and predictability, and its role in the Earth system through climate–carbon cycle feedbacks operating across timescales from days to millennia. A central objective is to improve the representation of marine carbon, nutrient cycling and microbial processes in Earth System Models while increasing spatial model resolution to capture key physical and biogeochemical dynamics in the ocean.To support this mission, we are seeking different Scientific Programmers (m/f/d) to drive the next generation of ocean biogeochemical modelling in Earth System Models. The successful candidates will contribute to the development, integration, and performance optimization of a state-of-the-art modelling framework, enabling increasingly sophisticated representations of marine biogeochemical processes and unprecedented high-resolution numerical experimentation. Together, they will help ensure that the modelling infrastructure combines scientific excellence with cutting-edge software engineering, delivering robust, efficient, and scalable performance on current and future exascale computing platforms.The successful candidate will help ensure that the modelling framework of the HAMburg Ocean Carbon Cycle model (HAMOCC) which is part of the ICON Earth system modeling framework remains technologically advanced and capable of efficiently exploiting emerging HPC architectures. Emphasis will be placed on heterogeneous computing and the optimal use of CPU and GPU resources to maximize model performance, scalability, and portability.A particular focus of the position will be a dedicated project to prepare, optimize, and benchmark the code for deployment on heterogeneous CPU/GPU systems, ensuring efficient performance and supporting the transition to next-generation HPC infrastructure.The role involves close interactions with researchers, research students and model developers to translate scientific advances into reliable and maintainable model code. The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to peer-reviewed publications and present research outcomes at scientific conferences.Key responsibilities:- Develop and optimize model code of HAMOCC for modern supercomputing architectures- Enable and improve heterogeneous execution across CPUs and GPUs- Lead and contribute to software development, maintaining Git repositories, testing and debugging, code review, and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) to ensure robust, maintainable, and reproducible code- Implement performance analysis, profiling, and optimization strategies- Support portability across current and future HPC platforms- Collaborate with model developers to translate scientific requirements into efficient software solutionsDesired qualifications:- Degree in computer science, computational science, applied mathematics, or a related field- Experience with numerical modelling and analysis and handling of large simulation datasets- Strong knowledge of HPC programming (Fortran and C/C++) and performance optimization- Knowledge of parallel programming paradigms such as MPI, OpenMP, OpenACC or equivalent technologies- Experience with large-scale scientific software projects, including software testing and debugging, code review workflows- Strong knowledge of software engineering best practices, including Git- Fluent in English, with solid scientific writing skills and a strong interest in working collaboratively within an international and interdisciplinary teamWhat we offer:This position is initially offered for three years. Continuation beyond the initial term is intended, subject to satisfactory performance, applicable legal requirements, and the availability of funding.We offer a position in an international science environment. You can expect a multifaceted job with challenging tasks in an exciting, academic work environment. You will have a high degree of autonomy and creative freedom, and we will promote your further education, e.g. within the framework of external courses and certifications. The compatibility of private life, family and career are important components of our personnel policy. You will be paid according to the collective agreement for the public service (TVöD Bund). Allowances are possible depending on qualifications and areas of responsibility.Are you interested?We look forward to receiving your full application via our online application portal. This should include a statement of interest, CV, publication list (when applicable) and a list of references (with contact information). Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applications received by 15 September 2026 will receive full consideration; applications received after that date may be considered until the position is filled.The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more disabled individuals and especially encourages them to apply. The Max Planck Society strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds.We are looking forward to your application!Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Meeresbiologie

jobs.description: Become a part of our journey and join the Constructor Community as:PhD Researcher (m/f/d): AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content GenerationYou are expected to contribute to the development of internationally visible, foundational research in AI-driven semantic structure extraction, automated reasoning-flow modeling, and adaptive content generation. This includes work on semantic parsing, structured NLP, graph-based neural models, metacognitive prompting, ontology alignment across disciplines, and human-in-the-loop optimization.In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged—particularly collaborations spanning computer science, computational linguistics, cognitive science, and the learning sciences. You will contribute to developing datasets, baseline models, personalized learning engines, reasoning-graph representations, cross-domain mapping algorithms, and RLHF-style feedback loops that improve system interpretability and instructional quality. The successful candidate will also contribute to high-quality publications, release research prototypes, and support demonstrator systems that deliver structured semantic extraction, rationale-aware content generation, and cross-domain transfer of reasoning structures.Additionally, the successful candidate is expected to support teaching activities in areas such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, AI in Education, Knowledge Representation, and Python-based analytical seminars at the BSc, MSc, and PhD levels. Responsibilities include assisting in course delivery, advising students, supervising Bachelor/Master theses, and engaging in methodological innovation for online, hybrid, and in-person learning environments. The university provides strong support for early-career researchers, including mentorship, administrative assistance, access to computational resources, conference funding, and opportunities to collaborate with other research groups and industrial partners working at the intersection of AI and digital education.Your Profile- Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.- Strong research interest and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: - semantic parsing and structured representation learning- knowledge graphs or graph-based reasoning- transformer models, sequence modeling, or GNNs- natural language generation and explainability- educational AI, personalization algorithms, or cognitive modeling- Evidence of research potential through publications, a strong thesis, or significant projects.- Experience or interest in innovative teaching and learning approaches.- Ability to translate theoretical insights into engineered prototypes and systems supporting scientific or educational use cases.- Responsible, self-motivated, and capable of working independently as well as collaboratively.- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.- Intercultural competence and experience in international environments.- Fluency with co-pilot tools for coding and writing.- Fluency in English, the language of instruction and communication on campus.Funding & Appointment TermsThe appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:- Monthly stipend of €1,650- Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)- Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month- Supplementary €550 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)Application Details- Expected start date: February, 2026Application package must include:- Curriculum Vitae (CV)- Academic transcripts- A detailed letter of motivation outlining research interests and career goals- 2 recommendation lettersApplications to be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.

jobs.description: About the roleJoin us as our Team Lead Technical Operations and help shape the reliability, resilience, and future of DIGITEC’s SaaS operations!DIGITEC is a leading provider of Foreign Exchange SaaS solutions, specializing in FX Swaps, NDFs, and Money Markets. We are looking for an experienced and hands-on Team Lead Technical Operations to lead our TechOps team and ensure the reliable, secure, resilient, and scalable operation of our D3 SaaS platforms .In this role, you will combine technical leadership, people development, and operational ownership, leading a multinational TechOps team of four people based across Hamburg, London, and Singapore. Reporting directly to the CTO, you will play a key role in evolving our operations from manual and infrastructure-centric processes toward a more automated, standardized, observable, and cloud-native environment, applying SRE and Operational Excellence principles.You will work closely with DevOps, Development, Security, Product, and Service Delivery to continuously improve how we operate our platforms and deliver reliable services to our clients.Your ResponsibilitiesTechnical Operations & Reliability• Lead the reliable, resilient, secure, and scalable operation of our D3 SaaS platforms.• Drive service reliability using SRE principles, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, observability, and reliability engineering.• Oversee incident, problem, and escalation management while strengthening Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, and technical resilience.Operational Excellence & Transformation• Drive the evolution toward automated, standardized, observable, and cloud-native operations.• Continuously improve operational processes, tooling, automation, and KPIs to increase reliability and efficiency.• Promote a culture of Operational Excellence, continuous improvement, and effective problem management.Team Leadership & Collaboration• Lead and develop our multinational TechOps team across Hamburg, London, and Singapore, fostering ownership, collaboration, and continuous learning.• Provide technical and operational direction while remaining hands-on where needed.• Work closely with DevOps, Development, Security, Product, and Service Delivery to align priorities, solve operational challenges, and continuously improve our services.Preferred qualifications• Several years of experience operating business-critical SaaS and cloud applications, combined with proven leadership experience in technical teams.• Strong hands-on experience with SRE and Operational Excellence, including observability, SLIs/SLOs, automation, operational KPIs, and continuous improvement.• Solid experience with incident, problem, and escalation management in production environments.• Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure, DevOps practices, networking, operating systems, and containerization.• Good knowledge of Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, technical resilience, and security principles relevant to SaaS operations.• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical and business teams.• A hands-on and proactive mindset, with the willingness to understand the technical details of our D3 product family.• Fluent English skills.Nice to have Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage:• ITIL certification or practical experience with ITIL-based service management.• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Terraform.• Experience with AIOps, operational automation, or cloud-native transformation.• Experience working in regulated environments, ideally financial services.• German language skills.What we offer as an employer• Join an Innovative Leader: Be part of a pioneering SaaS tech company recognised as the global standard in its category, experiencing impressive double-digit annual growth.• Transform a Major Market: Contribute to our mission of revolutionising the FX Swaps market with cutting-edge solutions and technologies.• Be part of an international work force: Work within a truly multi-national team, collaborating with colleagues from across the globe, located in London, Hamburg, and Singapore.• Make an Impact: Hone your skills in small teams where your ideas matter, actively shaping your role and driving your personal growth.• Enjoy Competitive Benefits: Benefit from a competitive compensation and benefits package, including 30 days of annual paid leave.• Invest in Your Development: Access a €1,000 (or equivalent in local currency) yearly budget dedicated to further education and professional development.Our commitment to inclusion:We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, genders and identities, and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive teamAbout usDIGITEC Financial Technologies and Services GmbH stands at the forefront of the financial technology sector, renowned for developing cutting-edge software solutions. Our innovative products encompass a wide spectrum, from pricing and settlement solutions for FX/MM businesses to FX market data services. With over 40 prominent banks worldwide, spanning Europe, America, Asia, and Australia, among our esteemed clientele, we have solidified our position as a global leader.At the heart of our success is our exceptional team, comprised of approximately 80 dedicated professionals boasting expertise in software development, financial mathematics, sales, IT systems, and more. Operating from three key locations—Hamburg (headquarters), London, and Singapore—we champion equal opportunities and foster a culture of respect and collaboration, ensuring a welcoming and supportive work environment for all.Join us as we continue to redefine the landscape of financial technology with DIGITEC.

jobs.description: In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number ofPhD positions.- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department is headed by Ramin Golestanian and hosts a number of group leaders, postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.The researchThe PhD students will engage in theoretical and/or computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter, under the supervision of Ramin Golestanian. German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary and working hours are in accordance with the funding guidelines of the Max Planck Society for junior scientists. Working hours are fulltime; salary is 2/3 of E13 TVöD-Bund. The starting date is flexible.The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. jobs.description: Job posting no. 20261009The GWDG is seeking aStorage Expert (m/f/d)to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C) with a regular working week of 39 hours (100%). Remuneration is in accordance with the collective agreement for the German public service (federal government); depending on qualifications, the position will be grade TVöD E 13. The position is suitable for part-time work and initially limited till 31rd December 2029. The GWDG strives for long-term cooperation. If interested, there is the possibility of a doctorate.The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG operates the HLRN-IV system “Emmy”, one of the most powerful computers in the world.As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG offers technical support to researchers and students from various science domains using sophisticated computer codes, including earth system science, life science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. At the same time, we aim to improve our close collaboration with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), and specialized computing centers including the German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ) and the Institute for Advanced Simulation Jülich (IAS-JSC).As part of our AI Service Center for Sensitive and Critical Infrastructure (KISSKI) we have created a number of AI-based services that offer high levels of security and privacy due to being processed on our own hardware. The position will be located within the subproject “KISSKI-EvoKS” and closely collaborate with customers from SMEs and Startups to develop prototypes and workflows that lead to PoCs and Blueprints. Those customers will come predominantly from sectors with high data protection requirements.The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, AI, and Machine Learning.ResponsibilitiesWe have a wide range of potential responsibilities that we would like to discuss with you. Your responsibilities in our team could include, for example:- Design, implement, and optimize high-performance storage solutions tailored for AI and HPC workloads- Conduct research on scalable, cost-effective storage architectures suitable for AI training and HPC simulations in resource-constrained environments- Develop and deploy data management strategies for large-scale AI datasets, including data lifecycle management, versioning, backup, and security (e.g., GDPR-compliant data handling)- Investigate and prototype AI-optimized storage systems leveraging technologies such as NVMe, SSD caching, and distributed storage (e.g., Ceph, MinIO, Lustre)- Support SMEs in evaluating and selecting appropriate HPC and AI storage solutions- Collaborate with data scientists and engineers to ensure storage systems meet the demands of AI model training, inference, and real-time processing- Develop best practice guidelines and toolkits for SMEs to manage AI/HPC data efficiently and security- Provide technical advisory and training to SME teams on data storage, performance monitoring, and data governance- Monitor and benchmark storage performance, ensuring low latency, high throughput, and cost-efficiency for AI/HPC applicationsRequirements- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related field- Experience in HPC systems, storage infrastructure, and AI data engineering- Proven experience with high-performance storage technologies (e.g., Lustre, GPFS, Ceph, NFS, S3-compatible storage)- Strong knowledge of AI/ML data pipelines, including data ingestion, preprocessing, and model training workflows- Hands-on experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and orchestration tools in HPC/AI environments- Familiarity with cloud storage platforms- Experience in data lifecycle management, data versioning, and metadata management- Solid understanding of data security, privacy (GDPR), and compliance in AI applications- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills- Excellent communication skills and ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders- Very good German skills (C1)- Very good English skills (C1)- Willingness to travel on businessDesirable- Experience in research or innovation projects related to HPC, AI, or data infrastructure- Knowledge of AI-driven storage optimization (e.g., predictive data placement, auto-tiering)- Familiarity with open-source HPC/AI frameworks (e.g., Slurm, Singularity, MLflow, Kubeflow)- Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash) and system administration (Linux/UNIX)Our offer- Flexible working hours and opportunity for mobile working- A modern, diverse, and exceptional work environment with close proximity to academia and research at the intersection of several innovative technology sectors- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center- Collaboration in a competent and committed team- Qualification and further development of your skills- Social benefits of the public sectorYour applicationHave we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 08.11.2026 via our online form:Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:Doctoral research associate for BabylAXO detector developmentLimited: 3 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FHDO021/2026 | Deadline: 02.11.2026 | Full-time/Part‑time | Remote work possibleDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.The Cluster of Excellence "Quantum Universe" performs research to understand mass and gravity at the interface between quantum physics and cosmology. The research team includes leading scientists from mathematics, particle physics, astrophysics, and cosmology at the University of Hamburg and DESY. As part of the cluster's experimental program to search for hypothetical very lightweight bosons, for example motivated by dark matter and dark energy in the universe, the construction of the BabylAXO experiment will start shortly. BabylAXO will look for axions and similar particles emitted by the sun in uncharted parameter regions. The doctoral research associate will engage in the start-up phase of BabylAXO and work on the extension of its scientific portfolio.The successful applicant will be attached to the ALPS group at DESY, which together with international partners is realizing new experimental facilities to search for new kinds of very lightweight elementary particles, works on new concepts targeting high-frequency gravitational waves and developing related technologies. Doctoral research associates will become members of the Quantum Universe Research School (QURS), which provides academic and key skills training, as well as career planning support. In addition, they will receive individual budgets to facilitate the attendance of summer schools and conferences, and to support other educational measures. Additional travel money for project-specific duties will be provided by the hosting research groups. Doctoral researchers may participate in teaching at the University and in the organization of the Cluster via an early career council.About your role:- Contribute to the commission and installation of the BabylAXO X-ray detection systems- Develop a calorimeter for BabylAXO sensitive to axions from solar fusion processes and supernova explosions- Explore synergies of the calorimeter development with medical applicationsAbout you:- MSc degree in Physics or equivalent qualification- Hands-on experience in the design, construction, commissioning, and operation of complex experimental setups- Programming experience in scientific computing environments- Independent, proactive, and goal-oriented working style with a strong commitment to solving complex technical challenges- Excellent written and spoken English skills- Experience in detector development for or operation of experimental particle physics or dark matter search experimentsGood reasons to join:Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. Remuneration is according to the regulations of the TV-AVH. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations.For further information, please contact Axel Lindner at +49 40 8998‑3525 (https://tel:+494089983525) (axel.lindner@desy.de (axel.lindner@desy.de) ).DESY in Hamburg does not grant doctoral degrees directly but collaborates with the University of Hamburg. jobs.occupation: PhD Position on Femtosecond Spectroscopy of Chiral Molecular Ions (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Job available in 2 locations: Bremen, KasselWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionA PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.About the TRILOGY Doctoral NetworkTRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.About the PhD ProjectThe selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.Key Research Activities- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.Candidate ProfileApplicants should have:- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection- Excellent written and spoken English.- Good written and oral communication skills.- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.MSCA Mobility and Eligibility RequirementsAs the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.Application DocumentsApplications should include:- Cover letter- Detailed curriculum vitae- Academic transcripts- Copy of the Master's thesis- Scientific publication, if available- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.Selection ProcessCandidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.Key InformationPosition: PhD Researcher / Doctoral CandidateNumber of positions: 1Research areas: Physics, Engineering, ChemistryResearcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)Contract: Temporary, full-timeWorking hours: 35 hours per weekCountry: GermanyWork locations: Bremen and KasselFunding: Horizon Europe – Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral NetworkProject: TRILOGYMarie Curie Grant Agreement: 101226887If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter.At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of  , color, religion, ___ ,   orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or any other legally protected status.Apply today! http://jobs.thermofisher.com (http://jobs.thermofisher.com)

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activity (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the field of solar physics and planetary research with around 300 employees. The interdisciplinary research focus is the investigation of the development, diversity and dynamics of planets, moons, small bodies, the sun and solar-like stars. The MPS develops and operates scientific instruments for current and future space missions (e.g. ESA, NASA), and carries out cosmochemical laboratory investigations of meteorites as well as numerical modeling on state-of-the-art supercomputers.The Department Solar & Stellar Interiors at MPS invites applications for the position of aPostdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activityIn recent years, exoplanetary science has undergone a major shift -- moving from exoplanet detection towards understanding star-planet systems as a whole, including the host star, interplanetary medium and galactic context. Specifically, tidal and magnetic interactions between planets and their host stars have been recognized to be able to modulate the evolution of both, including the atmospheric evolution of the planet and its habitability. The newly established ERC StG project PLANETARE seeks a postdoctoral researcher with a background in stellar magnetism and/or exoplanetary science to develop novel ways of detecting and characterizing the mutual influence of stars and planets with a focus on the influence of planets in short orbits on the magnetism of their host stars. At the core of the project is a new way to find exoplanets: detecting them through their magnetic interaction with the host star. This position builds the observational foundation - the sample, the activity catalog, and the geometry of the systems - and confirms any transiting planets among the interacting systems.Your Tasks- Compile the most accurate and complete flaring activity catalog to date using space-borne photometry- Search the sample of flaring stars for transiting planet candidates using space-borne photometry- Constrain the orientation of the rotational and magnetic axes of interacting systems- Measure stellar activity characteristics and their predictive power for interactionThe transit search, flaring catalog and geometry measurements will constrain some of the drivers of interaction and its observability, working towards a true occurrence rate of magnetic interaction in young star-planet systems. You will work closely with a second postdoc (https://karriere.mps.mpg.de/jobposting/ff58b9b82b6efc0b224bf8134f1471929fdc639c0) within a small, newly formed team of two postdocs and a PhD student, led by the PI (Ekaterina Ilin). jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to detect exoplanets through magnetic star-planet interaction (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the field of solar physics and planetary research with around 300 employees. The interdisciplinary research focus is the investigation of the development, diversity and dynamics of planets, moons, small bodies, the sun and solar-like stars. The MPS develops and operates scientific instruments for current and future space missions (e.g. ESA, NASA), and carries out cosmochemical laboratory investigations of meteorites as well as numerical modeling on state-of-the-art supercomputers.The Department Solar & Stellar Interiors at MPS invites applications for the position of aPostdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to detect exoplanets through magnetic star-planet interactionIn recent years, exoplanetary science has undergone a major shift -- moving from exoplanet detection towards understanding star-planet systems as a whole, including the host star, interplanetary medium and galactic context. Specifically, tidal and magnetic interactions between planets and their host stars have been recognized to be able to modulate the evolution of both, including the atmospheric evolution of the planet and its habitability. The newly established ERC StG project PLANETARE seeks a postdoctoral researcher with a background in stellar magnetism and/or exoplanetary science to develop novel ways of detecting and characterizing the mutual influence of stars and planets with a focus on the influence of planets in short orbits on the magnetism of their host stars. At the core of the project is a new way to find exoplanets: detecting them through their magnetic interaction with the host star. This position develops the detection method itself, i.e., the statistics, the search, and the physical model behind it.Your Tasks- Develop new statistical techniques to identify signatures of planet-induced flaring- Identify young stars and search them for planet-induced flaring using archival and upcoming Kepler, TESS, and PLATO observations- Measure how the strength and frequency of planet-induced flaring change as systems age- Develop a forward model of the magnetic feedback loop between planet and starThe derived occurrence rates of planet-induced flaring constrain the prevalence of interaction; the modeling of the evolution and mechanism will be built on the largest survey for planet-induced flaring to date. jobs.description: About usAirbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.Job descriptionIn order to support the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department, Airbus Operations is looking for aMaster student (d/f/m) in the field of Aerodynamics in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics departmentYou are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of a job title? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department as a master student (d/f/m)!- Location: Hamburg- Start: 01.06.2025- Duration: 6 monthsYour opportunity- Are you passionate about aircraft physics?- Are you keen to master the way we compute external loads acting on the vehicle due to maneuvers, flight in turbulence, landing impact, ground-handling?- Do you like to work in an empowered manner?- Do you enjoy connecting people and collaborating with many different interfaces?- This job will give you the opportunity to work internationally with several internal flight physics departments and with teams located in Europe and India.About usWe are a team of 16 multicultural and passionate engineers who perform the gust calculations for overall aircraft design for all aircraft types. Our team is involved from a very early design stage until certification and also in-service support. We are responsible for running build model activities such as finite element modeling, creating mass and aerodynamics models. We perform gust loads calculation, including failure cases, and deliver to internal interfaces. On top, we are deeply involved in research and technology aspects with new aircraft configuration assessments, model based system engineering, automation and machine learning.IntroductionThe current industry approaches of modeling unsteady aerodynamic flow for the prediction of gust loads typically assume linear flow conditions. Linearity greatly reduces the computational time required to evaluate all the flight points and gust conditions required by the certification specifications (CS-25). At the same time, disregarding non-linearities such as boundary layer separation arising from the high angles of attack induced by strong gusts can lead to an over-estimation of loads and thus to an increased structural weight of the aircraft.Your locationYou will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.Your benefits- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilitiesDuring this six months Master thesis you will develop and evaluate an unsteady aerodynamic model that includes the effect of flow separation in a piecewise linear approach. The model will be built using linearized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of a complete flexible aircraft and adapted using aerodynamic data obtained in the non-linear flow region at high angles of attack. You will evaluate the model by comparison against higher-fidelity models, such as obtained from non-linear time domain simulation, with respect to gust loads.You will contribute to:- Optimize the design of Airbus commercial aircraft in the frame of new wing technologies- the development of new approaches to model unsteady aerodynamics considering non-linearities for gust loads and flutter computation- Actively support us as a new member of our team on our journeyDesired skills and qualifications- You are a fulltime enrolled master student (d/f/m) within Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent- You have good knowledge in aerodynamics, CFD and potential flows- Ideally you already have first experience in CFD using TAU or CODA- You have knowledge in coding using Python and/or Matlab- You bring basic knowledge in overall aircraft design and basic competencies in flight loads calculation and flight mechanics- You are passionate to understand physical aspects and to use your engineering judgement- If you are familiar with tools like MSC.NASTRAN or ALTAIR HyperWorks, this is beneficial- You are a highly motivated, proactive and open-minded person with a great sense of initiative- You are keen to deepen your technical knowledge while enjoying to work in a multicultural team- Your English is at negotiating levelPlease upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match? In the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, researchers from the Social Sciences and Humanities as well as artists explore the relationships between technology, science, and society. The Lab was initiated by The Schaufler Foundation together with TUD Dresden University of Technology. The Lab's guiding theme for the upcoming third funding phase (April 2027–September 2030) is "Energy Cultures in Transition". The guiding theme is investigated from a humanities, cultural, social, and educational science perspective, explored through artistic practice, and communicated to the public. For the third funding phase, the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden comprises eight doctoral fellowships and an annually changing Artist in Residence program.TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.The Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden offers, subject to the availability of resources, aDoctoral Fellowshipfor a period of 2 years, with the option of extension by 1.5 years, starting on April 1, 2027. The fellowship (EUR 1,850 per month, plus a grant for material costs of EUR 150 and, where applicable, a family supplement of EUR 315 per child) is aimed at early-career researchers in the field of Sociology. Primary supervision will be provided by Prof. Dr. Susann Wagenknecht, Chair of Micro-Sociology and Technosocial Interaction.The guiding theme Energy Cultures in Transition understands energy as a cultural phenomenon deeply inscribed in aesthetic, historical, political, ecological, economic, and socio-technological practices and systems. Building on the dynamically growing research fields of the Energy Humanities, Science & Technology Studies, and the Digital Humanities, the aim is to examine how modern energy regimes—from petromodernity, to nuclear culture, and post-carbon futures—have shaped not only material infrastructures but also subjectivities, power relations, progress narratives, geopolitical orders, ecologies, and knowledge systems, while simultaneously being shaped by them. Interdisciplinary perspectives from the social sciences, cultural studies, humanities, and educational research represented at the Schaufler Kolleg@TU Dresden enable the analysis of the multifaceted entanglements of energy, culture, and society. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the field of Sociology, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- The (conflict-ridden) negotiation of imaginaries, infrastructures, institutional frameworks, and/or externalities (e.g., emissions, waste, waste heat) associated with energy production and supply across a wide variety of practices, communities, networks, organizations, markets, fields, and/or assemblagesTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the discipline of Sociology. The fellowship requires a high degree of willingness to engage in interdisciplinary dialogue, particularly with the STEM partnerships of the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, as well as to conduct joint research with artists within the framework of the Schaufler Residency. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Participation in the Kolleg's English-language training program is mandatory.Requirements:You hold an excellent university degree in Sociology or a comparable field in the social sciences, as well as relevant previous experience in the sociological analysis of the environment, technology, or energy, and/or in the field of Science and Technology Studies. You have a strong ability to work in teams and enjoy interdisciplinary collaboration. As the training program is conducted in English, you have English skills at a minimum of C1 level. In accordance with the doctoral regulations of the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Science, the dissertation may be written in either German or English—if you choose to write it in German, corresponding German language skills are required. Beyond this, German language skills are desirable but not mandatoryWe offer:The opportunity to pursue a doctorate within the Schaufler Kolleg with a structured qualification program and integration into an interdisciplinary research project. You will receive a fully equipped office workspace on the premises of TUD and access to an excellent research infrastructure, including participation in Research Studios and writing retreats. The Graduate Academy and other central institutions of TUD offer numerous further training and qualification opportunities. In addition, within the limits of the available project funds, the Schaufler Lab will cover the costs of conference travel. Inclusion and equal opportunities are important to us. We therefore look forward to receiving applications from people regardless of gender, origin, sexual orientation, worldview, or disability. TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The University is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment. The fellowship does not constitute an employment relationship.Application: Your detailed application, in German or English, should contain, in addition to the completed online application form (https://tu-dresden.de/gsw/schauflerlab/schaufler-kolleg/phase-3/anmeldung-registration) , a letter of motivation, a curriculum vitae in tabular form including an account of your academic career, a copy of your most recent university degree certificate, an exposé of your research project including a work and time schedule (max. 20,000 characters). Please send us your application documents, including the online application form, quoting the reference number s26-008, by November 24, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de/)  by sending it as a single pdf file to schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, Prof. Dr. Susann Wagenknecht, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .
